title: Reflection
context: What is reflection in Java, and what are its costs?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Reflection lets code inspect and use classes, fields, methods and constructors at run time through `java.lang.reflect` and `Class`. Frameworks use it for dependency injection, serialization and test runners. Its costs are slower calls than direct code, weaker compile-time checks, and broken encapsulation, because `setAccessible` can reach private members. On modern JDKs, module rules limit that access to open packages.

points.title: What it is for
points.why: Frameworks use reflection to wire and create objects from class metadata.

points.title: Costs
points.why: Reflection is slower, bypasses compile-time checks, and can break encapsulation.
